D.treatment: HIV and AIDS education intervention programme

O.outcome_detail: perceived HIV knowledge across HIV and AIDS topics

cells.quote: Perceived HIV knowledge increase was evident: pathophysiology (n = 93, 70.2%); immunology (n = 97, 72.9%); transmission (n = 116, 87.5%); diagnosis (n = 109, 81.8%); prevention strategies (n = 118, 88.4%); staging and monitoring (n = 106, 80%); pre- and post-test counselling (n = 104, 78%).
cells.note: The entry reports descriptive demographics, and the study uses a descriptive quantitative design with no control group or pre-intervention comparison. The reported knowledge percentages are self-reported perceived knowledge, so a treatment-versus-comparison direction cannot be established.

O.outcome_detail: perceived HIV and AIDS knowledge gained

cells.quote: Perceived HIV knowledge increase was evident: pathophysiology (n = 93, 70.2%); immunology (n = 97, 72.9%); transmission (n = 116, 87.5%); diagnosis (n = 109, 81.8%); prevention strategies (n = 118, 88.4%); staging and monitoring (n = 106, 80%); pre- and post-test counselling (n = 104, 78%).
cells.note: The study reports post-programme perceived knowledge among 133 students but does not report a control group, pretest, or other valid comparison. Participants were second- to fourth-year university students, and programme exposure ranged from 1 to 3 years.
